value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Round-11 fix (thread PRRT_kwDOVPw2oc61YZyq on the SDK adoption PR), class rule: a shape-based exemption in the credential fast path must be at least as strict as the documented safe set it carves out; content that does not match the documented shape must fall through to the full literal policy, never be blanket-accepted. Fixed instances of the class: (1) credentialLiteral exempted every /^<[^<>]*>$/ value, so a generic credential wrapped in angle brackets (a synthetic password literal in JSON) skipped the length rule and was stored; the exemption is now restricted to recognizable placeholder shapes (redacted, or letter-only words joined by spaces, underscores or hyphens). (2) The class search found the same bracket blindness in the free-text assignment rule: its assigned-value charset excludes angle brackets and the quoted-key signal path never sees unquoted keys, so free-text forms (colon or equals, quoted or bare) hid bracketed credentials entirely; a wrapper-aware scan now routes the bracketed value through the same credentialLiteral policy. Documented placeholder shapes (<redacted>, <secret-manager-reference>, letter-word phrases, uppercase) remain accepted; digits, symbols, provider tokens and credential material in brackets refuse; prose angle brackets without a credential key are unaffected. docs/sdk-adoption.md states the restricted placeholder contract.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Round-14 fix (thread PRRT_kwDOVPw2oc61eP9E, blocking). Class rule: a quote is surrounding syntax, never a reason to stop or exclude the interior of a recognized credential wrapper. Fixed instances: the free-text bracket scanner excluded quotes from the wrapper interior, so password assignments whose bracketed value contained a single or double quote were stored; the same scanner also required an unquoted key, so a quoted key with a quote inside the brackets truncated before the credential policy. Both now use one wrapper scan that keeps the full bracket interior and accepts a quoted key. The JSON scalar path already decoded internal quotes and was not a second implementation. The unquoted token scanner still stops at a quote because that quote starts another token and there is no wrapper to recover; that is a different rule. Markdown link parsing is not a credential scanner. Docs state the contract. Packed npm and bun consumers share this in-process scan.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Revert proofs in a disposable copy, restored afterwards: reverting only the bracket interior from any non-bracket character back to excluding quotes fails the quote-position control (1 failure: a quote inside the brackets is stored). Reverting only the quoted-key visibility fails the same control (1 failure: a quoted key whose bracketed value contains a quote is stored). Restoring the scanner passes the control. The control inserts each quote style at the start, middle and end of a credential and checks bare, equals, quoted-value and quoted-key forms, while recognized placeholders and prose quotes stay accepted.
